_note: Which crawler belongs to which website — the global list, so pasting a URL can say 'we know this one'. `script` is relative to this directory (`crawlers/`), so `known/storya.lua` is `crawlers/known/storya.lua`; an empty `script` is a site we know about but have no crawler for (the caveat says what blocked it). `language` is not trivia: the voices and the G2P are Vietnamese, so an English chapter is silently mispronounced until someone reads this field. This registry is deliberately not exhaustive and not auto-updating — it is the set this project has actually verified, and a missing site is a site nobody has written down yet. Embedded at compile time (see bm-core's crawl/known.rs), so a script named here that is not on disk is a test failure rather than a crawl that quietly runs without selectors.

sites.shape: `/{book}/chuong-{n}` — templatable, one fetch a chapter. The crawler the pipeline shipped before scripted crawls existed, still bundled and parity-tested; a new workspace names no crawler at all.
Templatable, but the chapter *list* is paginated — `discover` walks the page links.

`/{book}/chapter-{n}-{title-slug}.html` — the number is in the URL but not last, so nothing can invent the slug. The book page also lists only the first ~30 chapters with no pagination, so `discover` walks the `next_chap` chain instead.
English, slug discovery over the catalogue's 14 chapter columns.
sites.language: English — but `/vi/` is the Vietnamese edition of the same catalogue
sites.caveat: Refused behind Cloudflare: 403 whatever we send. The template is correct and cannot be run without a `cf_clearance` cookie in `crawl.headers`; a browser User-Agent alone does not get in.
Answers 200 with a Cloudflare interstitial rather than a 403 — the one shape that reads as success. `bm-inductor check` is what tells the two apart.
A Next.js app: the chapter is fetched by JavaScript and is not in the HTML at all. Needs a browser, which this crawler deliberately has not.
